verdict.rationale: Apple's own tech-specs page publishes a concrete memory bandwidth for M4 Max (546GB/s on the 16-core CPU/40-core GPU configuration), and the Mac Studio newsroom piece corroborates 'over half a terabyte per second'. The pack contains no vendor-stated memory type and no M4 Max capacity ceiling: the 512GB figure is for M3 Ultra, and the 'nearly 200 billion parameters' claim gives no number. So only one of the three sizing inputs is documented. Missing for 10: published memory type (e.g. LPDDR generation), M4 Max unified memory capacity ceiling, bandwidth for other M4 Max bin configurations, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can size memory-bound workloads from the vendor's own numbers — published memory type, capacity ceiling, and bandwidth (or spec detail complete enough to derive it)
